products.name: Workday AI
products.note: HR and finance AI; skills-based talent; predictive analytics; sensitive HR data exposure

profile_text.body:
Workday describes itself as an enterprise AI platform for HR, finance, and IT. On its own site the company presents Sana and agentic AI as a new way to work, saying its AI lets customers activate teams of specialized agents to carry out key processes across HR, finance, and IT. Workday says its agents can find, build, act, and automate rather than only assist, and it frames the pitch around turning AI into ROI faster, with trust, agility, and data readiness.

The company's tracked AI offering is Workday AI, described as HR and finance AI covering skills-based talent and predictive analytics, with sensitive HR data exposure noted as a consideration. Workday is a public company founded in 2005, headquartered in Pleasanton, California, and traded as WDAY. Its most recent revenue filing is a 10-K for the period ending 2026-01-31, reporting $9,552,000,000, and its CIK is 0001327811.

Workday is a defendant in a set of federal cases. Meckfessel Poletti v. Workday, Inc. appears in the District Court, E.D. California, and Williams v. Workday, Inc. in the District Court, N.D. Georgia. Elias v. Workday, Inc. is in the District Court, N.D. California, and Hill v. Workday, Inc. appears in both the District Court, D. Maryland and the District Court, E.D. Virginia. Noriega (PS) v. Workday, Inc. and Doe (PS) v. Workday, Inc. are both in the District Court, D. Colorado. Litigation exposure is concentrated in California, with 281 cases there.
